title: GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, and Kimi K3 released in July 2026
description: Major AI model releases in July 2026 include OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family (Sol, Terra, and Luna tiers), xAI's Grok 4.5 for coding and agent tasks, and Moonshot AI's Kimi K3. The LLM ecosystem now tracks over 500 models across commercial APIs and open source releases. Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Fable 5 continue to be major players in the AI coding space.
author: LLM Stats

title: July 2026 AI Price War: Grok 4.5, GPT-5.6, and Muse Spark 1.1 Redefine Enterprise Costs
description: Massive price war in July 2026: SpaceXAI, OpenAI, and Meta shipped new flagship models within 24 hours, igniting fierce price competition. Grok 4.5 costs $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. OpenAI's Luna lands at $1 for input and $6 for output. Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 runs at $1.25 for input and $4.25 for output. These prices are 5% of the cost of legacy flagships like Opus 4.8 ($25) and Fable 5 ($50). The models converge on agentic workflows designed to run tools and operate software rather than just answer questions. Anthropic responded by resetting all rate limits for users in a defensive move.
author: Kersai

title: Meta Shifts from Open-Weight to Closed Paid Models with Muse Spark 1.1
description: Meta made the largest structural shift in July 2026 by launching Muse Spark 1.1 as their first paid closed model, ending years of dominating the open-weight AI space with the Llama series. This signals that giving away frontier models for free is no longer sustainable when value shifts from model weights to agentic execution layer. Running parallel subagents and maintaining million-token contexts requires expensive inference infrastructure that open-weight sponsorship can't sustain. For the open-source community, this leaves a vacuum that GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek must fill.
author: Kersai

title: DeepSeek Designs Custom Inference Silicon to Break Free from Nvidia and Huawei
description: On July 7, 2026, Reuters reported that DeepSeek is designing its own AI chip targeting inference to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei. The chip is about a year old and still in early stages, with DeepSeek in talks with chip designers, foundries, and memory suppliers. However, US export rules requiring TSMC, Samsung, and SK Hynix approval before providing controlled technology to China present major hurdles. This signals broader decoupling: the AI hardware stack is bifurcating into a US-aligned ecosystem relying on Nvidia and a China-aligned ecosystem building domestic alternatives.
author: Kersai
